newsitem.title: USA: Yellen - CPI shows no apparent U.S. price pressure.
newsitem.headline: Yellen - CPI shows no apparent U.S. price pressure.

text.p: The White House's Council of Economic Advisers Chairwoman Janet Yellen said Wednesday that the latest consumer inflation data show the U.S. economic expansion continuing with no apparent pressure on prices.

"Combined with recent news on producer prices and retail sales, today's consumer price numbers indicate that the expansion is continuing at a sustainable rate with no apparent pressure on prices," Yellen said in a statement.

The Labor Department reported on Wednesday that consumer prices during the first half of the year rose at their slowest pace in 11 years. The Consumer Price Index, the government's most widely used inflation gauge, rose a smaller than expected 0.1 percent in June for the fourth month in a row, the department said.

The so-called core rate of inflation, excluding volatile food and energy costs, also rose only 0.1 percent last month, the department said. In the first half of 1997, the core rate rose at a 2.4 percent annual rate, the slowest in 32 years.
"This report, together with last Friday's report on producer prices, indicates that inflation rmains well under control," Yellen said.
